title: GitHub Copilot: Complete Guide
description: Master GitHub Copilot — from basic tab completions to chat, inline edits, and agent mode. Learn the prompting techniques that get the best results.

data.text: GitHub Copilot is the most widely adopted AI coding assistant, with millions of developers using it daily. It comes in several flavors: inline code completions as you type, a chat panel for conversational coding help, inline edit suggestions for selected code, and increasingly, agent capabilities that can plan and execute multi-step changes.

data.title: Getting started takes just a few minutes:
items: Install the GitHub Copilot extension in VS Code, JetBrains, or Neovim
Sign in with your GitHub account and activate a Copilot plan (Individual, Business, or free for students and open source contributors)
Open a project — Copilot automatically detects the language from your file extensions
Start typing and accept suggestions with Tab

data.text: Getting the Best from Inline Completions

data.title: Tips for high-quality suggestions:
items: Write clear, descriptive function and variable names — Copilot reads them as context
Add comments above the function stub describing what it should do
Keep related code in the same file when possible — Copilot uses the open file as context
Accept or reject suggestions quickly; the model improves its suggestions based on your patterns

data.text: Copilot Chat is a separate panel where you can have a conversation about your code. Select code, right-click, and ask "Explain this" or "Refactor this to use a Map". You can also ask about code in other files, ask for test generation, or request architectural advice.

data.title: Slash commands save time
data.text: Copilot Chat supports slash commands like /explain, /fix, /tests, and /doc. Type / in the chat input to see available commands. These trigger specialized prompts that produce more reliable results than free-form chat.

Copilot Edits lets you select a block of code, describe the change you want in natural language, and see the proposed edit inline. This is ideal for refactoring tasks — select a 50-line function, type "break this into three smaller functions", and Copilot will rewrite it in place.

Copilot's agent capabilities are evolving quickly. In agent mode, Copilot can read multiple files, plan a series of changes, execute them, and check the results. This is the most powerful but also the most experimental feature. Start with chat and inline edits before relying on agent mode for production work.

data.title: Review agent output carefully
data.text: Agent mode makes multiple changes across files in one go. Always review the diff carefully before accepting. Look for unintended changes to files you did not intend to modify.

GitHub Copilot sends snippets of your code to the server for processing. For enterprise users, there are options to keep data in your environment. For individual users, code snippets are used to improve the model unless you opt out. Be aware of this when working with proprietary code or sensitive data.

data.title: Effective Copilot Chat prompt
data.content:
Instead of: "Fix this function"

Try: "The fetchUserData function below throws an unhandled error when the API returns a 404. I want to handle 404 gracefully by returning null, and let other errors propagate. Use the existing handleApiError utility in src/utils. Keep the function signature the same."
data.code:
// Prompt:
"The `fetchUserData` function below throws an unhandled error when the API returns a 404. I want to handle 404 gracefully by returning null, and let other errors propagate. Use the existing `handleApiError` utility in src/utils. Keep the function signature the same."

data.title: Copilot quick-start checklist
points: Install the extension and sign in
Enable suggestions in your preferred languages
Try slash commands in chat for structured tasks
Use inline edits for selected-block refactoring
Use agent mode only after reviewing simpler features
